answer: A farm emitting 37 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the reef panel. Because the entropy is measured at the tide gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the raven audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 27 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
